Q156.question_text: Express \(\log_3 54 + \log_3 6 - \log_3 12\) as a single exact logarithm. [WMA12 P2, 3 marks]
Q156.explanation: Apply the addition law of logarithms \(\log_a x + \log_a y = \log_a(xy)\) to the first two terms M1 [1]: \(\log_3(54 \times 6) = \log_3 324\). Apply the subtraction law \(\log_a x - \log_a y = \log_a(\frac{x}{y})\) to combine with the third term: \(\log_3(\frac{324}{12}) = \log_3 27\) M1 [1]. The exact single logarithm is \(\log_3 27\) A1 [1].

Q158.explanation: Integrate term by term: \(\int (2x^3 - 4x + 1) dx = \frac{x^4}{2} - 2x^2 + x\) M1 [1]. Apply the limits 1 and 3: \([\frac{x^4}{2} - 2x^2 + x]_1^3\). Substitute the upper limit 3: \(\frac{81}{2} - 2(9) + 3 = 40.5 - 18 + 3 = 25.5\) M1 [1]. Substitute the lower limit 1: \(\frac{1}{2} - 2 + 1 = -0.5\). Subtracting the lower value from the upper gives \(25.5 - (-0.5) = 26\) A1 [1].

Q163.question_text: Solve the equation \(\cos(x - 30^\circ) = 0.5\) for \(0^\circ \leq x < 360^\circ\). Give exact degree values. [WMA12 P2, 3 marks]
Q163.explanation: Let \(Y = x - 30^\circ\), so the range for Y is \(-30^\circ \leq Y < 330^\circ\). Solve \(\cos Y = 0.5\) M1 [1]. The principal angle is \(60^\circ\), and the second solution in the range is \(360^\circ - 60^\circ = 300^\circ\), so \(Y = 60^\circ, 300^\circ\) M1 [1]. Convert back to x by adding \(30^\circ\): \(x = 90^\circ, 330^\circ\) A1 [1].
